articles.title: Bill Maher Fires Back at Trump by Comparing Him to Taylor Swift
articles.content: Bill Maher learned that when it comes to Donald Trump , no good deed goes unpunished. On last week’s episode of “Real Time with Bill Maher,” the political pundit defended his recent White House dinner with the president, exclaiming, “You know what? Fuck you. I like these dinners,” before conducting an embarrassingly chummy interview with Trump’s former press secretary, Karoline Leavitt . Despite all his brown-nosing, Trump lashed out at Maher in a 1,300-word Truth Social tirade Sunday night, calling the comic a “complete and total loser” and “major POTHEAD” who “looked like hell” during their dinner this month, where they were joined by ESPN pundit Stephen A. Smith and former rapper Kid Rock. Trump also claimed that Maher had begged him for years to go on his HBO show, but he “will never watch it again, because it is nothing more than FAKE NEWS that America, and the World, is unfortunately subjected to.” Related Stories Disney Broadens Super Bowl LXI Plans With Pat McAfee, Next-Gen Stats NFL Introduces Celebrity Guest Cheerleaders: On the Sidelines With Comedian Atsuko Okatsuka and the L.A. articles.title: Watch the ‘Rehearsals for a Revolution’ Director and Editor Explain How Memories Can Help Fight Authoritarianism
articles.summary: At our Art of the Doc event, director Pegah Ahangurani and editor Arash Ashtiani went deep on one of the year's most acclaimed films.
articles.content: Pegah Ahangurani’s “ Rehearsals for a Revolution ” is one of the year’s most powerful films, combining half a century of Iranian history with the director’s own personal story of being exiled to London. It all forms one powerful tapestry that begins with a single word: “Yad.” The Persian word for memory and remembrance ties the entire film together, allowing Ahangurani and editor Arash Ashtiani to weave timelines together under the idea that memory is its own form of revolution. At our Art of the Doc event in Los Angeles, the duo sat down with IndieWire editor-in-chief Brent Lang for a wide-ranging conversation that began with the film’s opening word. Related Stories ‘Who Killed Alex Odeh?’ Review: A Scattered but Searing Documentary Examines America’s Tacit Acceptance of Anti-Arab Discrimination Carrie Coon on ‘The Liberation,’ Life After ‘White Lotus,’ and Why Hollywood ‘Places Limitations’ on Actors — ‘Screen Talk’ Podcast Interview “I wanted to emphasize the act of remembering, because the central idea of my film is about remembering,” Ahangurani said. “I grew up in Iran and I’ve lived there my whole life, and I know very well that the authoritarians, including the one in Iran, they don’t only censor people. They also try to erase our memories, erase our past, and replace it with their own version of history. They try to rewrite it, and we shouldn’t let them steal our memories. I think remembering is one of the few things we have. We should remember our past, we should remember our victims, we should mourn them. Only after that can we start to heal.” National Geographic Documentary Films, part of a joint venture between The Walt Disney Company and the National Geographic Society, is committed to bringing the world premium, feature documentaries that cover timely, provocative and globally relevant stories from the very best documentary filmmakers. Its award-winning and critically acclaimed films reach 300 million people worldwide in 180 countries and 33 languages

articles.content: “ Criminal Minds: Evolution ” will end with its upcoming 20th season on Paramount+ , Variety has learned. articles.title: The 1973 ‘The Wicker Man’ Is a Classic, but Neil LaBute’s Loathed 2006 Remake Is Even Better
articles.summary: In a Halloween-week edition of the "Correct Opinion" column, we take a look at a rare remake of a classic that's superior to the original — not that you would have known it from the reviews.
articles.content: Reader, you have been lied to! Film history is littered with unfairly maligned classics, whether critics were too eager to review the making of rather than the finished product, or they suffered from underwhelming ad campaigns or general disinterest. Let’s revise our takes on some of these films from wrongheaded to the correct opinion . When filmmaker Neil LaBute signed on to write and direct a remake of the 1973 horror film “ The Wicker Man ” in 2006, both his fans and his detractors were surprised. Not that LaBute would be making a horror movie — after all, “In the Company of Men,” “Your Friends and Neighbors,” and “The Shape of Things” were all horror movies in a sense, disturbing pageants of trauma and sadism where the (human) monsters always won. Coming from a fiercely personal writer/director whose only previous studio assignment had been the handsomely mounted literary adaptation “Possession,” “ The Wicker Man ” seemed like an odd career choice. Was LaBute just broke, or did he inject his own preoccupations into Anthony Shaffer’s tale of a policeman whose missing-person investigation on a remote island leads to his doom? I don’t know if he needed the payday, but I do know that the answer to the second half of the question was a resounding “yes.” Not only is “The Wicker Man” pure LaBute through and through, but it’s also, like Brian De Palma’s “Scarface,” John Carpenter’s “The Thing,” or David Cronenberg’s “The Fly,” a rare remake of a classic that’s actually superior to its source. articles.title: LAPD Arrests 2 In Connection With Killing Of ‘SNL’ Writer Jimmy Fowlie’s Sister
articles.content: Nearly a year after she went missing, LAPD has arrested two people in connection to the death of Christina Downer, the late sister of Saturday Night Live writer Jimmy Fowlie . On Thursday, officers took 41-year-old Delorean Bijon Brandon, who is believed to be Downer’s boyfriend, and Kaylee Markowski, 34, into custody for allegedly murdering and disposing of her body, before concealing their involvement. Brandon and Markowski are both being held at Metropolitan Detention Center, where they have been booked on suspicion of murder and are both being held on $2 million bail. According to LAPD, Brandon claimed Downer had moved out of their home several months before her disappearance, leaving behind all of her belongings, including her vehicle and dog. Watch on Deadline Downer’s family reported her missing on Dec. 18, 2025, following a welfare check requested by her ex-husband after he hadn’t heard from her in an extended period of time. Detectives with LAPD’s Robbery-Homicide Division took over the investigation when her cellphone was discovered washed ashore on a Santa Monica beach. Last December, Fowlie sought help from friends and followers as he searched Downer’s Koreatown neighborhood, noting they were “worried that she isn’t safe.” Fowlie announced in April that LAPD had informed the family that Downer was “ no longer alive ,” and were treating the case as a homicide.

articles.title: Japan’s Film Funds Look Beyond Production Committees to Build New Financing Models
articles.content: Japan’s production committee system, in which a group of companies jointly finance a film and share its rights, has helped spread risk across the industry. But it can also cap budgets at what the industry itself can raise, make it harder for overseas investors to take part and slow decisions when every rights holder must agree. At a panel at TIFFCOM , the content market of the Tokyo International Film Festival , speakers examined whether film funds can ease those limits while still fitting Japan’s market. Kii presented K2P Film Fund I as one example of a new structure. The fund closed in February at about JPY5 billion ($32 million) and aims to back around 50 films over seven years. It is a blind pool, meaning investors commit money before the films are chosen. articles.title: Two Arrested in Murder of ‘SNL’ Writer’s Sister
articles.content: Two suspects have been arrested in connection with the murder of Christina Downer , “ Saturday Night Live ” writer Jimmy Fowlie ’s sister, according to the Los Angeles Police Department . Delorean Bijon Brandon, 41, Downer’s boyfriend, and Kaylee Nicole Markowski, 34, were arrested Thursday in Highland Park and Tarzana, respectively. Detectives believe Brandon and Markowski were responsible for Downer’s murder and then disposed of her body and concealed the crime. LAPD said law enforcement officials continued to investigate Downer’s disappearance after her cell phone washed ashore on the beach in Santa Monica. Authorities were led to search an Airbnb property in Joshua Tree, located in the high desert several hours from Los Angeles, in connection with her disappearance and conducted an extensive search with K-9 units and the San Bernardino County Sheriff’s Department. “Our prayers for her to be found safely have transformed into prayers for the truth to be revealed and for those responsible to be held accountable,” Fowlie’s post from April 29 read. “We have reason to believe that in the weeks before she went missing, her phone and social media were compromised. The individual(s) in possession of her phone used it to hide the fact she was gone, to ask for money and to create a false narrative that she was going ‘off the grid.’”

articles.title: Sourav Ganguly’s ‘Bigg Boss Bangla’ Among Highlights as Indian Media Giant JioStar Revenues Climb 10%
articles.content: JioStar , the Indian media giant backed by Reliance Industries, grew revenue from operations 10.1% year-on-year to INR68.1 billion ($710 million) in the July–September quarter despite a weak advertising market. Profit after tax fell 13.2% to INR11.5 billion ($120 million). Former India cricket captain Sourav Ganguly hosted the first-ever “ Bigg Boss Bangla,” which launched this quarter on streaming service JioHotstar . The reality franchise rolled out in six languages, and all editions together pulled in more than 90 million viewers in their first three weeks. That makes “Bigg Boss” the biggest entertainment property on the platform. Related Stories ESPN Launches ESPN JV YouTube Channel for Kids NFL to Face New Trial in Sunday Ticket Class-Action Lawsuit to Determine Financial Damages Reliance Industries credited JioStar’s revenue growth to subscriptions and to advertising on digital entertainment. Gross revenue rose 9.8% to INR79.4 billion ($829 million). Margins came under pressure. EBITDA from operations dropped 10.5% to INR13.7 billion ($143 million), and the margin fell to 22.1% from 28.1% a year earlier. A 36.6% drop in investment income pulled total EBITDA down 13.6% to INR15 billion ($157 million). The quarter was also well below April–June, when JioStar booked INR109.5 billion ($1.1 billion) in revenue from operations. JioHotstar averaged about 440 million monthly active users over the three months, up 10% on the prior year. In September, the platform relaunched under the JioHotstar name in the U.K., Canada and Singapore. Reliance said active subscribers in those three territories have grown about 30% since then. The company also introduced “Pay Kisi Aur Se” (“Ask Others to Pay”), which lets users send a subscription payment request to a friend or relative. Reliance said the feature raised payment initiations by 10%. Subscribers on mobile plans now get up to two hours a month of viewing on connected TVs. articles.title: Hotel and Travel Industry Groups Back U.S. Film Incentive as Tourism Draw
articles.content: Lobbying groups representing the hotel and travel industries have endorsed a 20% federal tax incentive for film and TV production, arguing that domestic filming attracts tourism from abroad. The American Hotel & Lodging Association and the U.S. Travel Association have joined an alliance of film industry stakeholders in pushing for the bill. The two groups represent airlines, ticketing sites, hotel companies and resorts, including the Disney and Universal theme parks. Related Stories Japan IP Market to Return to Cannes in 2027 as Tokyo Partnership Continues Guillermo del Toro Tears Up as He Says ‘We’re Handing Down a World in Ruins’: ‘It Pains Me Deeply to See Three Generations Fail the Next’ “Every film and TV production made in America sends a ripple through the travel economy, filling hotel rooms, restaurants and small businesses during the shoot and inspiring travelers to visit long after the credits roll,” said Geoff Freeman, president and CEO of the U.S. Travel Association, in a statement. “A federal production incentive would bring that economic activity back to communities in all 50 states and give destinations of every size a powerful new way to showcase themselves to the world.” A bipartisan group of lawmakers introduced the Motion Picture, Television, and Entertainment Revitalization Act last month. The bill would create a 20% tax credit for labor on film and TV productions in the U.S., with 5% bonuses for independent film and for filming in rural areas and disaster zones. The bill now has 52 sponsors in the House of Representatives and 10 sponsors in the Senate. The House sponsors are heavily concentrated in filming states, with 15 from California, six from Pennsylvania, four from New York, and three each from New Jersey, Illinois and Georgia. The House bill has been referred to the Ways and Means Committee, which handles tax legislation, while the Senate version is in the Finance Committee. articles.content: Carrie Coon , Mariana di Girolamo, Rosalind Eleazar , Jordan Firstman , Anthony Oppolito, Jaafar Jackson , Inde Navarrette and Kate O’Flynn, eight performers who have wildly different backgrounds but who each achieved a breakthrough in 2026 and now find themselves in Oscar contention, have been tapped to receive the Santa Barbara International Film Festival ’s Virtuosos Award in early 2027. Firstman, Ippolito and Jackson are in the best actor conversation for Club Kid , I Play Rocky and Michael . articles.title: Eric Karson, Director of ‘The Octagon’ and Producer of ‘Lionheart,’ Dies at 86
articles.summary: The son of a TV writer, he also worked with French kickboxer Olivier Gruner on two films and with Tom Skerritt on one.
articles.content: Eric Karson, the martial-arts movie specialist who directed Chuck Norris in The Octagon and produced the Jean-Claude Van Damme-starring Lionheart , has died. He was 86. Karson died Aug. 24 of natural causes while in hospice care in Henderson, Nevada, his brother Gil Karson told The Hollywood Reporter . Karson also directed Olivier Gruner in his first movie, Angel Town (1990), and produced his second film, Nemesis (1992), and the French kickboxer considered Karson a mentor. Related Stories Critic's Appreciation Patrick Stewart's Career Was a Rare and Thrilling Marriage of the Prestigious and the Populist Movies Patrick Stewart, 'Star Trek' Captain and 'X-Men' Superhero, Dies at 86 The son of a TV writer, Karson was working for Los Angeles-based American Cinema Productions when he was offered the chance to make his feature directorial debut on The Octagon (1980). Written by Leigh Chapman of Dirty Mary Crazy Larry fame at the dawn of the ninja movie craze, the film stars Norris as Scott James, a retired karate champion who takes on a band of assassins led by his estranged foster brother (Tadashi Yamashita). At Imperial Entertainment, Karson directed Van Damme in Black Eagle (1988), then reunited with the Belgian martial artist on Lionheart (1990), directed by Sheldon Lettich. With his turn as Lyon Gaultier, who deserts the French Foreign Legion and becomes a street fighter to raise money for his murdered brother’s family, Van Damme became a leading man in the U.S. One of four kids, Karson was born in Phoenix on March 5, 1940. His father was Lee Karson, who created the 1956-59 CBS-ABC program The Gale Storm Show (also known as Oh, Susanna ), set on a ship à la The Love Boat ; he also wrote for shows including The Restless Gun , Wagon Train and The Detectives . His mother, Mary, was a theater actress turned homemaker. The family moved to L.A. in the 1950s and lived in a house next door to John Wayne on Highland Avenue in Hancock Park. McHale’s Navy , starring Ernest Borgnine , Joe Flynn and Tim Conway , aired for four seasons (1962-66), and Wright appeared on all 138 episodes of the show that was set on the U.S. Navy boat PT-73 in the Pacific during World War II. He also appeared with the rest of the cast in the features McHale’s Navy (1964) and McHale’s Navy Joins the Air Force (1966). articles.summary: 'Hocus Pocus' and 'The Nightmare Before Christmas' also make their annual return to the movie chart.
articles.content: The midpoint of October brought with it a distinct turn toward Halloween and horror titles in Nielsen’s streaming ratings . The previous week’s No. 1 , Prime Video’s Carrie series, fell one spot but still took in more than billion viewing minutes. It was replaced at the top by another show with some horror/thriller elements, Netflix’s Below . Peacock’s Friday the 13th prequel series Crystal Lake debuted in the top five. Along with all that, Halloween movies Hocus Pocus and The Nightmare Before Christmas also made their annual return to the charts. Below logged 1.3 billion minutes of watch time in its second week, up a little from 1.19 billion minutes a week earlier. Carrie fell off by about 15 percent but still posted a strong 1.08 billion minutes. The Diplomat was the week’s biggest debut, scoring 983 million viewing minutes with the premiere of its fourth season. Crystal Lake followed on the original series chart with 774 million minutes (both shows premiered Oct. 15). A new season of Love Is Blind brought the Netflix series back into the rankings with 600 million minutes of viewing, tied with East of Eden . Apple TV’s Ted Lasso (546 million) stayed in the top 10 originals a week after its season finale. On the acquired series top 10, South Park (540 million minutes on Paramount+) made its first appearance this year midway through its current season. Ben Affleck’s Animals (756 million minutes) stayed on top of the movie chart for a second week. Hocus Pocus (209 million) and The Nightmare Before Christmas (173 million), both on Disney+, ranked fifth and seventh among films. articles.title: ‘Who Killed Alex Odeh?’ Review: A Scattered but Searing Documentary Examines America’s Tacit Acceptance of Anti-Arab Discrimination
articles.summary: Jason Osder and William Youmans’ film uses the "unsolved" murder of a Palestinian-American civil rights activist to explore how bigotry has become so normalized in this country.
articles.content: Times change, the arc of the moral universe bends towards justice, and yet one thing that has remained true for as long as I’ve been alive is that prejudice, bigotry, and explicit displays of racism have always been openly permissible in America — so long as they’ve been targeted at Arabs and/or Muslims. That sad and immutable fact was on full display throughout Zohran Mamdani’s mayoral campaign last year, and the say the quiet part out loud reaction to Abdul El-Sayed’s current senate race has somehow managed to be even worse on both sides of the aisle (Democrats lament that he “doesn’t share our values,” while Republicans straight up just call the guy a jihadist). But anyone old enough to remember 9/11 knows that it didn’t start with the likes of Vicky Paladino , just as I assume that anyone old enough to remember the assassination of Alex Odeh knows that it didn’t start with 9/11. articles.title: Carrie Coon on ‘The Liberation,’ Life After ‘White Lotus,’ and Why Hollywood ‘Places Limitations’ on Actors — ‘Screen Talk’ Podcast Interview
articles.summary: The charming "Gilded Age" star joins IndieWire's "Screen Talk" to discuss her magnetic performance as a Holocaust survivor, life as an actor on the "top of the B list," and her family's eclectic home viewing habits, including her husband, co-star Tracy Letts.
articles.content: The Emmy-nominated “White Lotus,” “Gilded Age,” and “The Leftovers” star has made plenty of impact on TV playing strong-willed characters. But she’s also a magnetic presence on the big screen, from films like Sean Durkin’s sizzling ’80s marriage satire “The Nest” and Azazel Jacobs’ Bergmanesque sibling drama “His Three Daughters” to her latest film , Guy Nattiv’s “ The Liberation .” In this film, she’s more vulnerable onscreen than ever. But as dark as Coon can go — in the ’80s-set “The Liberation,” she plays a repressed, PTSD-addled Holocaust survivor brought under the sway of a hypnotic cult leader played by Lily James — she’s a delight to chat with. No topics are off limits. That just means, though, because there are so few, there aren’t very many left over for the rest of us to take a crack at. So it is unusual for me to get this opportunity. I had an opportunity to play the lead in a mainstream film, which was ‘The Nest’ … and it came out during COVID, and nobody saw it. And so it didn’t necessarily open the doors we hoped. articles.title: ‘Ramayana: Rise of a Legend’ Review: India’s National Epic Gets a Fittingly Massive Cinematic Treatment
articles.summary: Nitesh Tiwari's Bollywood blockbuster will never bore you, even if you occasionally find yourself yearning for some quiet character development.
articles.content: In the hours before the review embargo for “ Ramayana: Rise of a Legend ” lifts, Google should see a massive influx of searches for “synonyms for epic.” It’s a reductive label: if you’re even remotely interested in a three-hour movie that covers half of a 1,500 page book spanning decades of war, romance, revenge, and interactions with the gods themselves, you already know that it’s an epic. But it nevertheless bears repeating and underlining, or at least replacing with all the variations of “majestic” and “monumental” that a thesaurus can provide. It’s hard to overstate just how big Nitesh Tiwari’s adaptation of India’s national epic really is. This is a film where Brahma himself, the Creator of the entire universe, makes an onscreen acting appearance before the 10-minute mark. Every facet of India’s topography, from lush grasslands filled with antelopes to gnarled forests with tigers and evil spirits lurking around every corner, is on full display. There are enough wars, musical numbers, “Gladiator”-style arena contests, talking eagles, lavish Indian weddings, Shakespearean feuds, da Vinci-esque flying machines, and shape-shifting to satisfy even the most attention span-challenged viewers. There are moments when Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” looks like “My Dinner with Andre” by comparison. articles.title: ‘Everest: The Other Side’ Review: A Grieving Ski Mountaineer Scales the Face of Death in Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin’s Climbing Doc
articles.summary: Haunted by tragedies this NatGeo doc never flinches at, Jim Morrison makes the dangerous attempt to climb up and ski down the Everest's North Face in another spellbinding chronicle from the Oscar-winning "Free Solo" team.
articles.content: A subject of considerable gossip in the documentary inner circle, the high-profile breakup of Oscar-winning mountaineer-filmmakers Jimmy Chin and Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi was bound to haunt their latest project, the exhilarating “ Everest: The Other Side ” for NatGeo. It’s the tense and vertiginously shot nonfiction chronicle of a grief-stricken alpine climber and skier, Jim Morrison, as he attempts to scale Everest’s North Face. To the naked eye, you can’t really say they’re using him as therapy. But aren’t they? Related Stories Bleecker Street CEO on Why the Social Media Suppression of ‘Musk’ Is About Much More Than Film Patrick Stewart, ‘Star Trek’ Legend and Beloved Shakespearean Actor, Dead at 86 Until Morrison’s record-breaking trek, only five people had successfully summited, and exactly zero had skied this Chinese-facing side of the world’s highest mountain. While history will tell you that Morrison safely hit his apogee and survived the project, the audience nonetheless remains in terrified, clammy doubt as Morrison endures unforgiving avalanches, a 9,000-vertical-foot corridor of bulletproof ice, and a shitstorm of personal tragedies in the run-up. Those tragedies include the dissolution of Morrison’s shared ambition to traverse the North Face when his partner (spoiler alert? Not really), elite ski mountaineer Hilaree Nelson, died in 2022. They had been preparing to take on the North Face during COVID when Nelson, skiing with her husband down the Manasalu summit in Nepal, was struck by an avalanche that caused her to fall approximately 5,900 feet. It’s a nightmarish, disaster-movie jump scare when a massive sheet of ice dislodges, taking Nelson down with it. Already, Morrison had brought heavy baggage worthy of its own emotional sherpa up the mountain: His first wife and his two children died in an airplane accident in 2011.
